concerns.text: Tasks T075-T085 (Review-Driven Operationalization) implement metrics (falsification, metabolic cost, irreducibility, etc.) that are NOT defined in spec.md FR-001 through FR-007 or SC-001 through SC-005. These tasks address reviewer concerns but lack a corresponding requirement in the spec, creating unapproved scope creep. The spec explicitly limits scope to FR-001..FR-007.

Tasks T000-FIX-SPEC and T000-FIX-PLAN instruct the implementer to edit upstream artifacts (spec.md, plan.md) directly. The spec and plan are source artifacts; tasks should not mandate editing them as part of the implementation workflow. This creates a circular dependency where the task list attempts to fix the spec that defines the task list.

Tasks T075-T085 reference specific reviewer concerns (Ada Lovelace, Turing, etc.) but these concerns are not formalized as requirements (FR/SC) in the spec.md. While the tasks exist, they are not traceable to a spec requirement, violating the coverage principle that every task must map to a spec element.

Task T004a-FETCH saves raw stream data but lacks explicit instructions to calculate and record the checksum in state/...yaml or data/manifest.json immediately, as required by Constitution Principle III (Data Hygiene) and spec.md Edge Cases. The task description is incomplete regarding data hygiene requirements.

Task T019a-TIE implements a fallback tie-breaking rule ('fall back to highest average confidence score') if the first path is invalid. However, spec.md Edge Cases explicitly mandate a deterministic rule ('prefer the first generated path') with NO fallback. This task description contradicts the spec requirement, creating a coverage gap where the task does not match the spec.

Task T018 requires outputting raw binning data to data/processed/ece_binning.json but does not explicitly mandate that this file be checksummed and recorded in the state YAML. This creates a gap in traceability for Constitution Principle IV (Single Source of Truth).
